# Reasons

Why a design system exists. Answered before any design decision.

## Business and product

Why the product exists and what it does for the business. It frames every later answer.

- **What does the product do for the business?** The main job of the product. Operating tools, publishing, selling and public services pull the system in different directions. Answers: Runs daily operations · Informs and publishes · Sells and converts · Serves the public. `business.q1`
- **How many brands or products share the system?** One brand keeps the system small. Many brands need a theming layer. Answers: One · A few · Many. `business.q2`

## People and work context

Who uses the product, how often and with what abilities.

- **Who uses it most?** The main audience. Experts learn an interface; occasional visitors must understand it at first sight. Answers: Daily experts · Occasional visitors · Everyone, including people with disabilities · Customers who choose us. `people.q1`
- **What accessibility level do we commit to?** The accessibility promise. It sets floors for contrast, targets and states. Answers: AA · AA, with AAA where it is cheap · AAA. `people.q2`

## Content and data

What fills the screen.

- **What is the main content?** Numbers, long text, forms and media each need different type, spacing and color. Answers: Numbers and records · Long-form text · Forms and tasks · Images and campaigns. `content.q1`
- **How much is on one screen?** Information density. It drives spacing, type size and how groups separate. Answers: A lot · A moderate amount · One idea at a time. `content.q2`

## Tasks and flows

What people do with the content.

- **What is the main task?** The task that must be fastest. Comparing, reading, completing and exploring need different layouts. Answers: Scan and compare · Read start to end · Complete a form · Browse and explore. `tasks.q1`
- **How often do people repeat actions?** Repetition. Frequent actions must be quiet and fast; rare ones can be explicit. Answers: Constantly · Sometimes · Rarely. `tasks.q2`

## Human factors

Attention, memory and effort.

- **What must the interface protect?** The scarce human resource on this product. Answers: People keep their place · Attention on the content · Low effort to understand · Delight. `human.q1`
- **How do people recall the interface?** Learned interfaces can rely on recognition. Fresh visits need explicit labels. Answers: They learn it and recognise it · They see it fresh each time. `human.q2`

## Outcomes

What success looks like and what failure costs.

- **Which outcome matters most?** The measure the system optimises for. Answers: Time on task · Reading comfort · Completion without errors · Engagement. `outcomes.q1`
- **What is a costly mistake?** The error the system must make hard. Answers: Acting on the wrong record · Losing your place · A task that fails · Looking off-brand. `outcomes.q2`

## Brand

How the brand should feel in the interface.

- **What should the brand feel like?** The feeling the interface carries. Answers: Precise · Warm · Calm and clear · Neutral and adaptable · Bold. `brand.q1`
- **How visible is the brand in the interface?** How much brand expression the product carries. Answers: Quiet · Present · Loud. `brand.q2`

## Use scenarios

Where and for how long people use the product. Written scenarios follow from these answers.

- **Where do people use it?** The place and device. A desk with a mouse, a phone on the move, or anything at all. Answers: At a desk · On the move · Anywhere, on any device. `scenarios.q1`
- **How long is one visit?** Session length. All-day use rewards learning; short visits must work at first sight. Answers: All day · One sitting · A few minutes. `scenarios.q2`

## Team and delivery

Who keeps the system right, and how fast it changes.

- **Who maintains the system?** Team size limits how many tokens and variants can stay correct. Answers: A small team · A platform team · An agency. `team.q1`
- **How fast does it change?** Change rate. Fast change needs a stable component API and a flexible theme. Answers: Rarely · Every month · Every campaign. `team.q2`
